supersedes: rc2-20260827 (md5 6d64126c80b86497c015774cb71c3bb4), on TIMING and on LVS VALIDITY, not on geometry -- the two submission streams are DRC-IDENTICAL: 1926 rulechecks, 737 results, 32 non-zero, ZERO differing, and rc1's submission matches both. WHAT CHANGED. rc2 was signed off against parasitics extracted at 25 degC for ALL THREE RC corners, because none of the create_rc_corner blocks carried -temperature (fixed in commit ec7948c). Extracting each corner at its own temperature, rc2 fails hold at three corners: -0.006/94 at the shipped corner, -0.078/22 at FF/1.32V/125C (a corner absent from the MMMC entirely), and -0.159/3 on reg2out once the hold libset's 0 degC IO library is corrected to the -40 degC one. rc3fix closes all three: +0.003/0, +0.003/0, +0.006/0, verified with all three hold views active. THE COST IS ONE SETUP ENDPOINT AT 1 ps. The bisection (hold_target_slack 0.000 / 0.010 / 0.020) establishes there is no target giving comfortable margin on both -- the design has about 13 ps to allocate. The allocation is deliberate: setup slack scales with the clock period and hold does not. -0.001 ns on a 10 ns cycle is 99.99 MHz; a hold failure is broken at every frequency and cannot be fixed after fabrication. At TYPICAL rc3fix reads setup +2.264/0 and hold +0.012/0 -- rc2 read hold -0.001/1 there, so rc3fix also fixes the typical corner. rc3fix is ALSO the first candidate whose LVS can detect a stranded power pin: it ran with the corrected .GLOBAL (commit 77f06a2), orphan /VSS source nets 18,322 -> 172, report 24.7 MB -> 1.59 MB.

known_bad.decision: NOT withdrawn and NOT rewritten. The digest is correct for what it computes and the raw md5/sha256 beside it are load-bearing -- a foundry Final Report cites the md5. Both edges RISING. The next path behind it is +0.011, a 12 ps gap, so this is ONE ISOLATED PATH and not a population. Setup passes everywhere else measured: +2.264 at TT/1.20V/25C and +0.044 at SS/1.08V/-40C.
known_bad.decision: CARRIED, with three independent reasons and one that is arithmetic. (a) SETUP SLACK SCALES WITH THE CLOCK PERIOD AND HOLD DOES NOT. -0.001 ns on a 10 ns cycle is 99.99 MHz instead of 100.00. Declaring 99.99 MHz makes the corner pass with no ECO, no re-stream and no re-verification. A hold failure is broken at every frequency and unfixable after fabrication. (b) THERE IS NO ALLOCATION THAT SATISFIES BOTH. Measured bisection on hold_target_slack: 0.000 gives setup +0.012 with hold -0.017/3; 0.010 gives setup -0.001 with hold +0.003/0; 0.020 gives setup -0.004/2 with hold +0.005/0. Interpolating to make both positive lands both within a picosecond of zero -- the knife-edge pathology a 72-configuration derate sweep spent a night diagnosing. (c) The part WORKS: at nominal conditions it has 2.264 ns of setup slack. This is a signoff miss at the worst-case corner, not a functional risk. UNTRIED LEVERS, recorded so this is a choice and not an omission: post-route useful skew has NEVER inserted anything on this design (grep FE_USK = 0) despite 5x-60x measured capture-side headroom on the setup-critical endpoints; and roughly 0.2 ns of the 0.35 ns setup clock uncertainty is duty-cycle distortion, which CANNOT reach a rising-to-rising check like this one. Both are next-run work: useful skew changes the clock tree, and the uncertainty change touches every path and must exclude the design's 226 negedge flops.
known_bad.withdraw_when: Withdrawn if the declared operating frequency is set to 99.99 MHz or below, at which point the corner passes arithmetically; or if a useful-skew or selective-uncertainty pass closes it with hold still >= 0 at all three corners.

known_bad.what: Voltus static rail on rc3fix's own database answers the question LVS on this design was structurally incapable of answering. instances_analysed 367,244 of 367,737 in the database -- the +1,504 ECO cells are ALL analysed and ALL reached. iv_disconnected_functional = 0. The 18 disconnected instances are FILL/DCAP endcaps in one contiguous pre-existing island, IDENTICAL in count to rc2, with zero logic cells. The 493 instances outside the analysis are the IO ring (VDDIO/VSSIO excluded by name), name-for-name the same as rc2's.
known_bad.decision: This is EVIDENCE, recorded here because it is the only power-connectivity evidence that exists for any candidate. It matters because before commit 77f06a2 this project's LVS could not detect a stranded PG pin at all -- its sign was inverted, and breaking a ground pin made LVS cleaner. SCOPE, stated: static at assumed activity, techonly PGV so cell internals are not modelled, die-only with no package model, and the IO ring is not analysed at all -- nothing in this project establishes that any IO cell reaches a VDDIO/VSSIO pad.
known_bad.withdraw_when: not a defect - this entry records a measurement and is withdrawn only if superseded by a rail run on a later database.
